content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
Site Reliability / DevOps Engineer | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused largely on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. Hands-on experience with GitLab CI, Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, plus personal experience building a k3s cluster and GitOps workflows. Uses Python, Bash and Java for automation and tooling. Currently studying for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and scripting: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Containers and orchestration: Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, k3s, Helm
CI/CD and GitOps: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Argo CD, Git
Infrastructure and operations: Linux, Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic), Hetzner VPS, AWS (EC2 and S3 basics for learning)
Monitoring and data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, as well as artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request test environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built test-result collection and Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests.
- Wrote Bash and Python tools for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and authored an internal guide to the CI system used in team onboarding.
- Work with namespace-level Kubernetes access; the platform team manages the shared cluster.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED PROJECTS

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, deploying applications from a Git repository with Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — studying; exam scheduled for January 2027

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
- Mentored two QA interns in 2023.
- Joined two incident calls as an observer; no production on-call experience.

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible and well-structured CV. It uses quantified outcomes effectively, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, lowering runner costs by approximately 30%, and reducing flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The experience demonstrates a logical progression from QA automation into CI/CD, test infrastructure and Kubernetes-adjacent work. The document is professional, readable and appropriately transparent about namespace-level Kubernetes access, personal infrastructure projects, CKA status and lack of production on-call experience. The main content concern is positioning: the headline may imply broader production SRE experience than the employment history demonstrates, although the summary itself provides useful context.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, chronological employment history, searchable technology names and simple text-based formatting. Relevant terms such as Python, Java, Git, GitLab CI, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, GitOps, Terraform, Linux, Prometheus and Grafana are present. The quantified achievements and project details should also perform well in AI-assisted screening. The main ATS limitation is that networking concepts requested by the advertisement—Ethernet, IP, TCP/UDP and routing—are not present, but the candidate's original information does not establish those skills, so they should not be added. Right-to-work status for Finland is also not stated and cannot be inferred or invented.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the technical foundation of the programme. Programming experience is shown through Python and Java; Git, containers, Kubernetes and GitOps are clearly demonstrated; and the personal k3s project provides relevant exposure to monitoring, ingress, TLS and infrastructure tooling. The candidate also demonstrates genuine learning and ownership through the homelab, Terraform project, CKA preparation, CI documentation and mentoring experience. However, the candidate's material does not establish current-student or recent-graduate status, and the candidate has not provided evidence of the right to work in Finland. With a 2018 degree and seven years of professional experience, eligibility for an early-talent programme may be a substantial issue. Networking fundamentals are also not demonstrated in the supplied material. Production SRE responsibilities, production on-call and direct cluster administration are not shown; the CV correctly avoids claiming them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR POSITIONING IMPROVEMENT: In the headline, replace "Site Reliability / DevOps Engineer | QA Automation Engineer" with a more precise formulation such as "CI/CD & Kubernetes Engineer | QA Automation Engineer" or "DevOps / Platform Engineering Transition | QA Automation Engineer". This preserves relevant SRE/DevOps keywords while avoiding an implication of established production SRE ownership that is not supported by the experience section.

MINOR STRUCTURE IMPROVEMENT: Rename the "ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE" section to "ADDITIONAL INFORMATION" because its contents include mentoring and incident-call participation rather than a separate employment role. Keep the two bullets, but make the evidence more searchable by changing them to: "Mentored two QA interns in 2023" and "Participated in two incident calls as an observer; no production on-call responsibility."
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- Site Reliability / DevOps Engineer

Genuine interest and basic knowledge of cloud platforms, operations, networking, hardware and software

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured and professional, with strong quantified achievements: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The experience and project sections provide credible evidence of a transition from QA automation into CI/CD, Kubernetes and platform engineering. The document also responsibly distinguishes namespace-level Kubernetes work from cluster administration and clearly labels personal learning, basic experience and the unpassed CKA exam. The main content limitation is that the opening positioning could align more directly with an early-career SRE/platform engineering programme rather than presenting the candidate primarily as a Kubernetes Engineer.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong. The CV uses conventional section headings, readable text formatting, standard date ranges, and keyword-rich descriptions including Python, Java, Git, GitLab CI, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, GitOps, Argo CD, Linux, Terraform, Prometheus and Grafana. The quantified bullets are also likely to perform well in AI-assisted screening because they demonstrate ownership and measurable impact. Screening probability is strong for programming, Git, containers, Kubernetes and GitOps, but weaker for networking fundamentals and Finnish work authorization because neither is established in the document. Avoid implying broader Kubernetes administration than the experience supports.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the technical direction of the programme. It demonstrates programming in Python and Java, familiarity with Git, containers, Kubernetes and GitOps, Linux exposure, CI/CD ownership, infrastructure learning and practical monitoring work. The homelab project is particularly relevant to Aurelis Cloud's engineering-first, learning-oriented environment. The candidate also shows documentation and mentoring experience, which supports the programme's emphasis on learning and knowledge sharing. The candidate's material does not establish current student or recent-graduate status, although the transition from QA automation into platform engineering can support the early-career-engineer route. Right to work in Finland is not stated. The material also does not demonstrate understanding of Ethernet, IP, TCP/UDP or routing, nor does it establish hardware experience. These are application gaps rather than CV wording defects and should not be invented or implied.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT — In the headline and Professional Summary, position the candidate more precisely as a QA automation engineer transitioning into SRE/platform engineering, rather than leading with "Kubernetes Engineer," which could imply responsibility for operating the shared cluster. For example, change the headline to "QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD & Platform Engineering" and change the opening of the summary to: "QA automation engineer transitioning into site reliability and platform engineering, with 7 years of experience including the last two focused largely on CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral test environments and build tooling." Keep the existing evidence about GitLab CI, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, k3s and GitOps immediately afterward.
